intent_snapshot.goal: Implement Slice S3 of Initiative lane-mode-followups: both Hosts accept a resume that passes lane_offers without max_parallel, the Pi max_parallel schema matches Claude Code's integer minimum 1, and the Pi loop surface registers lane-steward.

acceptance.assertion: Per Interfaces of docs/specs/parallel-batch-lanes.spec.md (Initiative parallel-batch-lanes) (source: repository evidence, Review of parallel-batch-lanes-s2-lane-integration findings review-1 and review-4): (a) a start_unattended_batch call with lane_offers and no max_parallel on a persisted v2 batch resumes it with the recorded max_parallel on both Hosts, and the same call on a batch with no v2 record is refused before any gate opens with a stable reason; (b) the Pi tool schema refuses a non-integer or sub-1 max_parallel at the schema, equal to the Claude Code input schema, with the typebox stub used by the packaged-tree tests extended if the chosen schema form needs it; (c) the Pi loop surface accepts lane-steward as a target and refuses an unknown target as before. Positive: Claude Code and Pi return equal reports for the same lane resume fixture. Negative: max_parallel 1.5, 0 and a lane_offers-only fresh start are refused before any gate; a resume with a different max_parallel is still refused with batch_parallel_mismatch. Bound: the declared tool parameters stay exactly initiative_slug, max_parallel and lane_offers and the generated Claude bundle matches a fresh generate. Agreed seams: tests/claude-batch-authority.test.ts, tests/pi-batch-authority.test.ts, tests/packaged-contract-tool-surface.test.ts, tests/imm-canary-work-contract.test.ts, tests/claude-host-package.test.ts.

attestations.summary: Both Hosts now resolve lane_offers-only calls through the shared resolveLaneParallel before any gate, the Pi max_parallel schema is integer-minimum-1, and the Pi loop surface registers lane-supply, which routes to lane-steward. The negative and parity tests sit at the agreed seams.

advisory_findings.summary: The acceptance text says the Pi loop surface accepts 'lane-steward' as a target. The Loop contract names the target 'lane-supply', which routes to the lane-steward role, and the change registers 'lane-supply'. That is the correct reading. A new test asserts the Pi LOOP_TARGETS list equals LoopRouteTarget, so the two cannot drift. The acceptance wording is imprecise but the implementation matches the contract.

evidence.trigger: A Pi loop call with target 'lane-supply' at Loop ownership reaches resolveLoopRoute and returns next 'lane-steward'. A Pi call with an unknown target is still refused by literalUnion(LOOP_TARGETS).

advisory_findings.summary: The agreed seams tests/packaged-contract-tool-surface.test.ts and tests/claude-host-package.test.ts are unchanged. The 'declared tool parameters stay exactly initiative_slug, max_parallel and lane_offers' and 'generated bundle matches a fresh generate' bounds therefore rest on those existing tests plus the Kernel QA pass. They are not strengthened by this diff. The Claude bundle diff does mirror the source change.

evidence.trigger: The change adds resolveLaneParallel to the bundled mcp-server.mjs and edits the Pi schema form. Neither of the two named package-level test files is touched.
